newsitem.title: USA: Egghead reports smaller loss after store closings.
newsitem.headline: Egghead reports smaller loss after store closings.

text.p: Egghead Inc., the retailer of computer software and hardware, Thursday reported a smaller loss in the latest quarter, with sales off sharply from a year earlier due to store closings.
It lost $3.6 million, or 21 cents a share, in its fiscal first quarter ended June 28, vs. a year-earlier loss of $7.5 million, or 43 cents a share.
Sales slumped to $56.1 million from $78.6 million.
Egghead said the weaker sales stemmed from its closing of 70 stores, which left a total 86 stores open, down from 162 in the year-ago quarter.

"We achieved our plan, which called for a significant reduction in operating losses," said George Orban, chairman. "We were able to do this by beating our expense plan and significantly broadening our merchandise offer."
He said that computer hardware and other non-software products represented 49 percent of the retailer's sales vs. 32 percent in the comparable period last year.

The company also announced that Steven E. Lebow and Linda Fayne Levinson have resigned from the board of directors. They will be succeeded by Greg Boudreau, chief executive officer, and Jon Brodeur, president, of Surplus Direct, which will merge with Egghead after stockholders approve the transaction in August.
Egghead's stock was unchanged at $5.25 on the Nasdaq market.
